ctx.x: Were people now asking you for a draw?

Yeah, in fact at Birdland I had Tommy Flanagan playing with me. And he calls me and he says, “I got a substitute coming in for tonight, his name is Roland Hanna.” I said, “Man I never heard of him.” He said, “Well, he’s a good player.” So I said, “Has he been around New York long?” He said, “No, I think he just came in from Washington or something.” When I went to club he was already there. He says, “Man, I’d like to get a draw.” I said, “Well I haven’t even heard you play, I don’t even know whether I’m going to…

items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: So I think my first was Jimmy Forrest, Joe Benjamin and Jimmy Jones was on piano... Anyway, they opened up with me.

ctx.x: Oh, yes, you almost wanted to --

Yeah, wanted to go to New York, anyway. So I think my first was Jimmy Forrest, Joe Benjamin and Jimmy Jones was on piano, and oh, what's the drummer's name in New York, not Elvin because Elvin came latter. He played with Billy Eckstine for a long time. Good drummer.* Anyway, they opened up with me. And it was a fantastic night, you know.
And Joe Benjamin, after he left, then I got Tommy Potter and Tommy Flanagan and Elvin Jones.

items.title: 69537_Jimmy Jones oral history interview
items.q: I think one night when Harry Edison came into the club, said, 'How did you get this guy to the house?'

ctx.x: Oh, the one that you had here in Los Angeles.
Yeah, with John. And it was great therapy for me at that time. I think one night when Harry Edison came into the club, said, 'How did you get this guy to the house?'
